instruction: Select the yellow triangle and position it in the top-right corner of the picture.

metadata.explanation: Task requires selecting the yellow triangle and moving it to the top-right corner of the image. The evaluator checks if the triangle's centroid is within 15% of the top-right corner position. Custom metric function check_triangle_topright__b91aae4ce11e76fbc123f25e08b42c98 finds the triangle using color-based segmentation and verifies its position relative to the top-right corner.

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly verifies the main requirement: triangle position in top-right corner using centroid calculation and tolerance-based checking
Postconfig properly exports the image to PNG for verification, ensuring state accessibility
Metric function correctly handles expected parameter when type='rule' by directly accessing expected.get('tolerance')
Triangle detection logic has a fragility: assumes 2nd most common color is the triangle without verifying it's actually yellow as specified in instruction
The 'position' key in expected rules is not actually used by the metric - function is hardcoded to check top-right, making the position parameter redundant
If the image contains multiple objects or complex backgrounds, the color-based detection (2nd most common color) could identify the wrong object
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add yellow color verification: check that the detected triangle color is actually in the yellow range (e.g., RGB checks or HSV color space filtering)
Make the metric function use the 'position' parameter from expected rules instead of hardcoding top-right, or remove the unused parameter
Add validation that the triangle_color is sufficiently distinct from background to ensure reliable detection
Consider adding a sanity check on triangle size/pixel count to ensure a valid shape was detected
